parties: Hybrid Financial Services Limited; K. Chandramouli
headline: K. Chandramouli files substantial acquisition disclosure in Hybrid Financial Services Limited
sum: K. Chandramouli has filed a mandatory disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations, triggering Regulation 31(4) reporting obligations in respect of Hybrid Financial Services Limited on the NSE.
implication: Disclosure under Reg. 31(4) flags a substantial acquisition crossing the 25% threshold or a material change in control intent; a partner reviewing this must immediately check the exchange filing portal for the full Form B disclosure to determine trigger event, target price, and conditionality framework.
detail: K. Chandramouli has submitted to the NSE a formal disclosure under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. The specific trigger event, consideration, and shareholding pattern are not disclosed in the headline notice; the full Form B and supporting schedules will be available on the NSE corporate actions filing portal. The filing indicates either a crossing of the 25% substantial acquisition threshold, an intention to acquire control, or a change in the acquirer's board representation intentions.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011
framework.note: Central: Reg. 31(4) mandates disclosure of substantial acquisitions and change of control; Reg. 4 defines 'acquirer' and thresholds (25%, 35%, 50%); Reg. 3 covers exemptions.
Central: disclosure to the company and its members of material changes in shareholding; s. 203 requires filing with MCA within prescribed timeframes.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, s. 11(2)
framework.note: Foundational: SEBI's rule-making authority and enforcement power over takeover disclosures.

framework.ref: National Stock Exchange (NSE) Listing Rules / BSE Listing Rules
framework.note: Central: exchanges prescribe continuous disclosure, prior intimation of substantial acquisitions, and dissemination timelines for Reg. 31(4) filings.
If acquirer is foreign or acquisition involves cross-border funding, RBI approval under FEMA may be required.
Stamp duty and transfer pricing implications if the acquisition triggers a change of control or involves non-resident entities.

framework.ref: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Master Direction – Acquisition and Takeover of Indian Companies, 2020
framework.note: If Hybrid Financial Services is a regulated entity (NBFC, banking, or insurance subsidiary), RBI prior approval under this direction may gate the acquisition.

conditions: Substantial acquisition crossing 25% shareholding threshold (presumed, pending full Form B)
Regulatory approval from RBI if Hybrid Financial Services is a regulated financial entity
Stock exchange approval and public announcement under SEBI Takeover Regulations
approvals: NSE (and BSE, if listed there) filing acceptance and continuous disclosure verification
RBI approval (if Hybrid Financial Services is a regulated NBFC, bank subsidiary, or holds a financial services license)
SEBI approval if any open offer is triggered
MCA filing under s. 203, Companies Act, 2013
structure.novel: No novel structure stated; standard substantial acquisition disclosure under Reg. 31(4).

triggers.law: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, Reg. 31(4)
triggers.note: Mandatory disclosure when acquirer crosses 25% or acquires control; triggers Form B filing and public dissemination via exchange.

triggers.law: RBI Master Direction on Acquisition and Takeover of Indian Companies, 2020
triggers.note: If Hybrid Financial Services is an NBFC, banking subsidiary, or other regulated entity, prior RBI approval is a gating condition.

triggers.law: NSE Listing Rules – Regulation of Substantial Acquisitions
triggers.note: Exchange-level disclosure and dissemination protocols; requires intimation before open offer or mandatory bid.

firms.note: Bar & Bench source does not identify legal counsel to the acquirer or target.
